votes.evidence: I traced the path from the webhook task through the carve-out to the resolver. Part of the premise holds: `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:144-156) returns None in two cases. One is when the toggle is off. The other is when `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (receivers.py:159-205) finds no artefact, unparsable JSON, no logins, or no org member. In both cases `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` returns `_InboxCarveOut(opted_out=True)` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:205-207). The skip path then chooses `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:897).
votes.refutation:
1) The copy is still true in the "unresolvable reviewer" case. The message (tasks.py:70-74) says "No reviewer currently has stamphog inbox reviews enabled for this self-driving PR, so stamphog will not re-review". When no reviewer resolves, no reviewer has the toggle on, so the message does not assert a false state. It also does not imply an author-trust problem, which is the reason the message exists (comment at tasks.py:67-68). `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` ("no longer qualifies for automatic review") would not be more accurate. The PR was positively identified as self-driving: bot author, repo-native branch, enabled config and a matching run (tasks.py:163-201).
2) The draft-flip claim is wrong. The dismissal at tasks.py:885-898 only runs when `action in _HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS`, and that set is {"synchronize", "reopened"} (tasks.py:49). The carve-out also returns empty for any other action except a base retarget (tasks.py:163-164), and a base retarget ("edited") is not in `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS`, so it never reaches this message. A ready_for_review or draft flip cannot post it.
3) The "reopened" wording issue is not new. The file already includes `reopened` on purpose, "defensively" (tasks.py:45-48). Every existing skip message says "New commits were pushed" on that same reopened path: `_LABEL_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:52-55), `_AUTHOR_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (57-60) and `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (62-65). The new message follows the established template.
What is left is a wording preference about a rare edge case: a self-driving PR that already has a stamphog approval but whose reviewers later stop resolving. It is not a correctness defect, and the approval is still dismissed correctly.

votes.evidence:
GA10 is not a real defect. At most it is a wording nitpick, and part of it is wrong.

1. **The reviewer case is not a false claim.** `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:151-156` does return None in two cases: when no reviewer resolves, and when the toggle is off. `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:205-207` maps None to `opted_out=True`. The resolver contract says this on purpose (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/inbox_hooks.py:19-20`: "else None (nobody resolvable, or the toggle is off)"). Before `opted_out` is set, the PR has been positively identified as a self-driving PR (`tasks.py:176-201`). If no reviewer resolves, it is still literally true that "No reviewer currently has stamphog inbox reviews enabled for this self-driving PR" (`tasks.py:70-74`). The generic `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` is the wrong alternative: the comment at `tasks.py:67-68` says it "would wrongly imply an author-trust problem".

2. **Draft flips cannot reach this path.** The dismissal runs only when `action in _HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` (`tasks.py:889`). That set is `{"synchronize", "reopened"}` (`tasks.py:49`). The carve-out also returns empty for any other action (`tasks.py:167-168`), so a draft flip never gets the opt-out copy.

3. **The "New commits were pushed" wording is shared, not new.** It opens every skip-dismissal message: `_LABEL_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (`tasks.py:52-55`), `_AUTHOR_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (`tasks.py:57-60`) and `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (`tasks.py:63-66`). The comment at `tasks.py:47-48` says `reopened` is included "defensively". A reopened delivery that dismisses an approval gets the same wording under every one of these messages.

4. **A test already covers this path.** `products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:791-826` has the resolver return None and asserts that the dismissal still fires with `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE`.

The approval is still dismissed in every case, so safety does not depend on the wording. What remains is copy nuance with no wrong behavior.
votes.refutation:
All three parts of the claim fail against the code.

- **Opt-out copy when no reviewer resolves:** the resolver contract deliberately folds "nobody resolvable" into None (`inbox_hooks.py:19-20`). The message stays literally accurate for a PR already identified as self-driving: no reviewer has the toggle enabled.
- **Draft flips:** the dismissal is gated on `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = {synchronize, reopened}` (`tasks.py:49`, `tasks.py:889`), and the carve-out returns empty for other actions (`tasks.py:167`). A draft flip never reaches it.
- **"New commits were pushed" on reopen:** every existing skip-dismissal message uses this lead-in (`tasks.py:52-66`), and `reopened` is included on purpose as a defensive case (`tasks.py:47-48`).

The approval is dismissed correctly in every case, and `test_tasks.py:791-826` covers this path. The finding is a copy preference, not a defect.

votes.evidence:
The skip path posts a dismissal comment only for `synchronize` and `reopened` events (tasks.py:49, :889). A draft flip (`ready_for_review`) never reaches it. The carve-out also returns empty for any other action (tasks.py:162-163), so `opted_out` is always False there. A base retarget comes in as `edited`, so it doesn't post this comment either.

The comment is posted only when a stamphog approval exists at a head other than the current `head.sha`. `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` (tasks.py:498-509) calls `dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head`, which filters `.exclude(head_sha=current_head_sha)` (approvals.py:52). If nothing is stale, nothing is dismissed and no comment goes out. So whenever the comment appears, the head really has moved past the approved commit, and "New commits were pushed" is true. That includes a `reopened` event. The same wording already exists in `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:63-66).

The other case is when no reviewer can be resolved. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` returns None when the artefact is missing, unparsable, or has no reviewer who maps to an org member (receivers.py:189-204), and the carve-out then sets `opted_out=True` (tasks.py:206-207). The message "No reviewer currently has stamphog inbox reviews enabled for this self-driving PR" is still literally true in that case: with zero resolvable reviewers, none has the toggle on. The PR has also already been confirmed as self-driving (tasks.py:175-200), so the message doesn't make a false trust claim. At most this is a wording nuance.
votes.refutation:
The first half of the claim can't happen as described. A comment saying "New commits were pushed" on a draft flip or a reopen with no new commits is never posted: draft flips don't take this path (only synchronize and reopened do, tasks.py:49/:889), and the helper dismisses only approvals from a different head sha (approvals.py:52). A reopen with no new commits finds nothing to dismiss, so no comment is posted.

The second half is not a correctness problem. When no reviewer can be resolved, "No reviewer currently has stamphog inbox reviews enabled" is still accurate, because there is no resolvable reviewer who has it enabled. The finding is a copy preference, not a defect.
